question: Given WB multimer bands + self-pulldown (NKG7 self-associates), do the predictors agree on HOW it self-associates?
finding: Yes - despite modest ipTM, all three C2 dimer models share a consensus interface core.
interface_location: N-terminus + TM1 (res 2-24) packing against the equivalent region of the partner, plus a TM2 contact (77,80,81). A lateral helix-helix (side-by-side) interface, NOT a ring around a central axis.
interpretation: WB/pulldown evidence that NKG7 oligomerizes is direct and outweighs predictor ipTM; 'no confident oligomer' was a statement about predictor confidence in interface GEOMETRY, not about whether NKG7 self-associates. NKG7 self-associates - confirmed.

The reproducible predicted interface is a lateral TM1-TM1 helix-packing contact (scaffold/lattice geometry), which is exactly why every model's pore is occluded: subunits pack shoulder-to-shoulder, not around an axis.
This is the SAME self-association mode shown by claudins, Ca_V/TARP-gamma, GSG1L and PMP-22 - all give multimer bands and self-coprecipitate, none is a channel on its own.
Oligomerization (supported by wet-lab) and pore-formation (not supported) are SEPARATE claims. The Tier-1 channel-specific conclusion is unchanged: the multimer NKG7 forms has no conducting pore.
